articles.headline: Forex reserves surge to record $740.8 billion
articles.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves hit a new peak of $740.8 billion by August-end, driven by record dollar inflows. This surge has helped the rupee strengthen by over 2.5% against the dollar since its June lows.

articles.headline: Tata Sons' stake in focus over RNT estate ruling
articles.summary: A Maharashtra charity commissioner's ruling raises questions over Ratan Naval Tata's estate, highlighting a condition that shares of Tata Sons must remain within the family or return to the trust. The stake is valued over $10,000 crore.

articles.headline: Beer volumes jump 17% as spirits market growth slows
articles.summary: India's beer market saw volumes surge 17% in Q1 FY27, while spirits grew only 2%, with state tax hikes making spirits more expensive and pushing consumers towards beer.

articles.headline: Sebi gives green light to NSE for $31.5k cr IPO
articles.summary: India's capital markets regulator Sebi cleared the NSE's $31.5k crore IPO, paving the way for the country's second-largest initial share sale. The nod follows the Supreme Court's acceptance of a settlement in co-location cases.

articles.headline: Maldives awards Thilafushi Port contract to China Co
articles.summary: The Maldives has awarded the Phase 1 contract for Thilafushi Port to a Chinese company, reneging on a joint development plan with India. This raises concerns about China's growing presence in India's neighbourhood.

articles.headline: Piyush Goyal urges companies to scale up social-impact projects
articles.summary: Commerce minister Piyush Goyal called for real inclusion to achieve Viksit Bharat by 2047 and urged companies to scale up social-impact programmes beyond CSR mandates.

articles.headline: Mathura, Vrindavan to get grand complexes like Ayodhya: Yogi
articles.summary: Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath announced plans to develop grand temple complexes in Mathura and Vrindavan on the lines of Kashi and Ayodhya, with central government support.

articles.headline: DJ ban during festivals divides Maha BJP, VHP
articles.summary: A controversy over bans on loud DJs during festivals has divided Maharashtra's ruling BJP and VHP, with local leaders vowing to defy restrictions. Violence erupted against those seeking a ban.

articles.headline: Naidu's long journey into 'Water Man' phase
articles.summary: N Chandrababu Naidu's inauguration of Polavaram and Poola Subbaiah Veligonda projects marks a shift towards being remembered as Andhra Pradesh's 'Water Man', focusing on water infrastructure.

articles.headline: New FTAs open big export gains across key sectors
articles.summary: Eight new FTAs signed in five years provide duty-free market access of $982 billion in electronics, $631 billion in agriculture, and $442 billion in gems and jewellery for Indian exporters.

articles.headline: I-T expands AIS to include GST returns, overseas investments
articles.summary: The Income Tax Department is broadening Annual Information Statements (AIS) to include GST returns, foreign remittances, and off-market securities transactions to curb tax evasion.

articles.headline: AI fuels low-value cybercrimes over high-value scams
articles.summary: The rise of AI is fueling low-value cybercrimes, with fraudsters using 'salami slicing' tactics to evade detection, targeting individuals instead of systems.

articles.headline: Rentomojo set to go public at $4,246 crore valuation
articles.summary: Furniture rental startup Rentomojo plans to raise $1,256 crore via IPO at a valuation of $4,246 crore, nearly five times its last private round valuation.

articles.headline: DeepSeek plans big Huawei AI chip order for data centre
articles.summary: DeepSeek plans to deploy 160,000 Huawei AI chips at a new data centre, potentially creating one of China's largest AI chip clusters and advancing its goal to replace Nvidia.

articles.headline: PVR INOX executive asked to leave after probe into alleged kickbacks
articles.summary: PVR INOX asked a senior executive to leave in April following an internal investigation into alleged kickbacks from developers, potentially involving up to $200 crore over several years.

articles.headline: HUL bets on brand push, cost cuts to revive growth
articles.summary: HUL targets 500 bps 'fuel for growth' via improved margins, efficiencies, and savings, redeploying gains into products, packaging, media, pricing, and channels.

articles.headline: Telco operators reject QoS norms for 5G slicing
articles.summary: Telecom operators like Jio and Airtel have opposed Trai's draft QoS norms for 5G slicing, arguing that resource utilisation benchmarks are arbitrary and would penalise efficient spectrum use.

articles.headline: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra raises bar for AI models
articles.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra reportedly outperforms rival models in coding, cybersecurity, reasoning, and more, potentially tipping the balance in AI development.

articles.headline: RBI turns to longer-dated VRRR for liquidity mop-up
articles.summary: RBI will hold a 30-day VRRR auction targeting $7 lakh crore to absorb excess liquidity in the banking system, which has surged to a record high of $10.3 lakh crore.

articles.headline: Govindas get bigger safety net this festive season
articles.summary: Insurance coverage for Govindas in Maharashtra has increased, with accidental hospitalisation cover doubled to $2 lakh and death benefit at $10 lakh, while keeping premium unchanged.

articles.headline: Trump gets August jobs boost before midterms
articles.summary: The US job market rebounded in August, adding 162,000 jobs, exceeding forecasts. The unemployment rate remained low at 4.1%, a potential positive for Trump before midterms.

articles.headline: Elon Musk 'PACs' $800k punch for Nov polls
articles.summary: Elon Musk's super PAC has spent over $800,000 to support Republican candidates in key congressional races ahead of the midterms, focusing on voter turnout efforts.

articles.headline: Bitcoin reclaims $80k despite choppy demand
articles.summary: Bitcoin briefly surpassed $80,000, its highest since May, as stock prices rose and the dollar weakened. The cryptocurrency's rally faces inconsistent demand from US investors.

articles.headline: FIFA accuses UEFA of 'smear campaign'
articles.summary: FIFA accused European football body UEFA of a 'smear campaign' in a court filing concerning FIFA President Gianni Infantino's failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup.

articles.headline: Sabalenka interrupts match over cannabis smell
articles.summary: World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka interrupted her US Open match due to a strong smell of cannabis, calling it 'disrespectful' to players. The scent has become a common complaint at Flushing Meadows.

articles.headline: POCO X8 POWER MASSIVE 10000 mAh BATTERY
articles.summary: POCO X8 POWER features a 10000 mAh battery, offering 3.5 days of power. It has a 1M+ Antutu score and India debut Qualcomm Snapdragon 6 Gen 5. Sale starts Sept 11 at ₹32,999.

articles.headline: EXTREME HEAT AND UNPREDICTABLE RAINS DISRUPTING TRADITIONAL CRAFT PROCESSES
articles.summary: Extreme heat and unpredictable rains are disrupting traditional craft processes and impacting livelihoods. Artisans face challenges in sourcing materials and maintaining quality due to climate change.

articles.headline: A soldier of action Adria Arjona fights super soldiers
articles.summary: New film 'Hit Man' stars Adria Arjona as a soldier fighting super soldiers, offering a blend of action and drama. The film is set to release soon.

articles.headline: Delhi Art Gallery, Mumbai Art Gallery to showcase collections
articles.summary: The Delhi Art Gallery and Mumbai Art Gallery are showcasing art collections from various artists, offering a glimpse into contemporary Indian art.

articles.headline: Indian E-way bills hit 77% of turnover
articles.summary: E-way bills have seen a 77% surge in turnover, indicating increased economic activity and compliance with GST regulations.

articles.headline: Tractor sales rise 33% to 1.1 lakh units in August
articles.summary: Tractor sales in India increased by 33% to 1.1 lakh units in August, driven by strong demand in the agricultural sector and favorable monsoon conditions.

articles.headline: Ultra-runners chase tough terrain
articles.summary: Ultra-runners are challenged by tough terrains in their pursuit of endurance and peak performance. The article highlights the physical and mental demands of ultra-running.

articles.headline: The trap of endurance
articles.summary: The article discusses the concept of endurance and its importance in life, highlighting the challenges and rewards associated with pushing personal limits.

articles.headline: A space of one's own
articles.summary: This article explores the concept of personal space and its importance in literary communities. It discusses how individual expression shapes literary narratives.

articles.headline: Sometimes crucial stardom is ineffable
articles.summary: The article reflects on the elusive nature of stardom and its impact on individuals. It delves into the complexities of fame and recognition in the entertainment industry.

articles.headline: Stuck in a loop of bad decisions
articles.summary: The article examines the consequences of poor decision-making, particularly in the context of the Nepal floods. It highlights the impact on livelihoods and infrastructure.

articles.headline: Changing climate tests craftspersons
articles.summary: Climate change poses significant challenges to traditional craftspersons. Rising temperatures, extreme weather events, and unpredictable rainfall disrupt their livelihoods.

articles.headline: An uncertain future for Assam's artisans
articles.summary: Assam's artisans face an uncertain future due to the impact of climate change and evolving market demands. The article highlights the challenges they encounter.

articles.headline: How to not reduce ridge cucumber
articles.summary: This recipe provides instructions on preparing ridge cucumber dishes, focusing on retaining its flavor and texture.

articles.headline: Traditional Indian method of creating and making
articles.summary: This article describes a traditional Indian method of crafting and making products, emphasizing sustainable practices and cultural heritage.

articles.headline: Two hydropower workers rescued alive from buried tunnel after Nepal floods
articles.summary: Rescuers pulled two workers, Kabir Maharjan and Sanjay Sah, alive from a debris-filled tunnel at the Trishuli 3A project on Friday. The survival comes ten days after catastrophic Himalayan flooding caused by a glacial collapse. Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha called it a miracle as search efforts continue for hundreds of others missing in several damaged hydropower sites.

articles.headline: IndiGo aircraft hits guidance pole at Srinagar airport; no injuries reported
articles.summary: An IndiGo flight from Navi Mumbai to Srinagar collided with a Docking Guidance System pole while taxiing into its parking spot at Srinagar International Airport. Officials confirmed that all passengers and crew members are safe with no injuries reported. The incident caused minor damage to the airport infrastructure during the parking process on Friday morning.

articles.headline: Delhi Arts Commission approves Manmohan Singh memorial at Rashtriya Smriti Sthal
articles.summary: The Delhi Urban Arts Commission has approved a proposal for a memorial dedicated to former PM Manmohan Singh. The commission directed that the architecture and landscaping must match the existing character of Rajghat. Authorities were told to ensure accessibility and use specific materials, and any significant design changes must be submitted for prior approval before execution.

articles.headline: Delhi Police detain content creator for assault after political protests
articles.summary: Delhi Police detained 21-year-old Swatantra Bhardwaj for allegedly injuring a man during a June protest at Jantar Mantar. The detention followed a protest by the Cockroach Janta Party. The victim, Sanjay Azad, suffered head injuries. Bhardwaj claimed he acted in self-defence and previously boasted of political ties. Police added SC/ST Act and POCSO sections following the incident.

articles.headline: National wrestler and children die in Maharashtra gorge jump incident
articles.summary: A 30-year-level wrestler and her two children died after jumping into a gorge in Dharashiv district, Maharashtra. One child survived with serious injuries and is under treatment. Police have booked the woman's husband and three in-laws for abetment of suicide and dowry harassment. The victim had reportedly been living with her parents following domestic disputes over money and gold.

articles.headline: Supreme Court rules heavy caseload no excuse for unreasoned judicial orders
articles.summary: The Supreme Court set aside an Allahabad High Court order, ruling that brevity cannot replace legal reasoning. The bench stated that judicial orders must demonstrate an application of mind to the facts. The case involved an HC order that failed to explain why six people were summoned for trial. The SC emphasized that reasons are essential for the unsuccessful party to challenge a verdict.

articles.headline: RBI to conduct Rs 7 trillion auction to drain excess cash
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India will hold a 30-day variable-rate reverse repo auction on Monday to manage a record Rs 10.5 trillion liquidity glut. The excess cash resulted from the RBI exchanging dollars from overseas Indians for rupees. The longer 30-day tenor aims to lock up banking cash for an extended period to curb inflationary pressures in the economy.

articles.headline: Heavy rains flood IGI Airport and trigger NCR traffic chaos
articles.summary: Sudden downpours left parts of Indira Gandhi International Airport waterlogged, forcing passengers to wade through ankle-deep water. At least 11 flights were diverted and over 400 delayed. Major routes like the Delhi-Gurugram expressway saw 10km traffic jams. The disruption comes just days before Delhi hosts world leaders for the Brics Summit, raising questions about infrastructure readiness.

articles.headline: ED seeks fugitive economic offender tag for ex-TMC leader Vinay Mishra
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate moved a Delhi court to declare former Trinamool Congress youth leader Vinay Mishra a fugitive economic offender. The agency seeks to confiscate his properties in cases involving alleged coal and cattle smuggling worth hundreds of crores. Mishra fled India in 2020 and acquired citizenship of Vanuatu. The tag allows for the seizure of his assets across the country.

articles.headline: British pharmacist to be extradited to India for arsenic poisoning case
articles.summary: A London court ruled that Ajith Kumar Mupparapu can be extradited to stand trial in India for allegedly poisoning his ex-wife’s family. Mupparapu is accused of killing his mother-in-law with arsenic-laced spices in Hyderabad in 2023. The judge found there was an arguable case against him, dismissing defense arguments regarding potential torture in Indian custody.

articles.headline: US regulators investigate Tesla Cybercabs over safety and steering compliance
articles.summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an investigation into Tesla’s new Cybercab taxis. Regulators are checking if the vehicles, which lack steering wheels, mirrors, and brake pedals, comply with federal safety standards for road deployment. The probe follows Elon Musk’s launch of the ride-sharing service in Austin, which uses two-seater autonomous vehicles.

articles.headline: India and Japan to play first Twenty20 International cricket match
articles.summary: India and Japan will face off in their first-ever men’s T20I cricket match on September 22 at Japan’s Sano International Cricket Ground. The match commemorates 75 years of diplomatic ties between the two nations. The BCCI stated that taking the reigning world champions to Japan marks a significant moment for introducing cricket to a wider audience in the Asian region.

articles.headline: Engineers use WhatsApp to guide trapped survivors in Nepal tunnel
articles.summary: A WhatsApp group with over 500 experts is providing technical drawings and real-time guidance to rescuers at flooded hydropower plants in Nepal. The digital collaboration helped locate tunnel entrances buried under millions of tonnes of debris. The effort led to the rescue of two workers from the Trishuli 3A project who had been trapped underground for nine days following a glacial collapse.

articles.headline: Over 3.6 million voter notices pending distribution in Karnataka revision
articles.summary: Data from the Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer shows 3.649 million notices for electoral roll revisions have not reached voters. The notices require electors to resolve logical discrepancies or prove citizenship. Hearings began on September 3 and will run until October 12. Officials are re-examining data to fix mapping errors that flagged families incorrectly before serving more notices.

articles.headline: Three booked for threatening private college students near Mangaluru
articles.summary: Police booked three individuals for allegedly abusing and threatening four private college students at a cafe. Two of the accused are alleged to be right-wing activists. The incident occurred on September 3 when the students were having breakfast. The accused reportedly questioned their presence and used verbal abuse. A complaint led to the registration of a case in Moodbidri.

articles.headline: Karnataka launches Rs 28.52 crore cloud seeding project for rain deficit
articles.summary: The Karnataka government launched a Rs 28.52 crore cloud seeding project to mitigate a rain deficit and avert drought. Water Resources Minister N Chaluvarayaswamy flagged off a light aircraft at HAL airport for the operation. The initiative targets areas with severe water scarcity. Previous operations had a success rate of 35%, and the state aims to safeguard farmer interests through this move.

articles.headline: Three suspended after Bagalkot school ceiling collapse injures eight students
articles.summary: Bagalkot authorities suspended an acting headmaster and two PWD engineers after a classroom ceiling collapsed on Wednesday. Eight students were injured, including one with a head injury. The headmaster was accused of failing to report the poor condition of the building, while the engineers were suspended for failing to ensure the school had a mandatory safety fitness certificate.

articles.headline: Karnataka minister urges industry to participate in Rs 241 crore ITI upgrade
articles.summary: Industries Minister M B Patil called for public and private sector participation in the PM-SETU scheme to upgrade 48 ITIs. The central and state governments are allocating Rs 210 crore, with industry expected to contribute Rs 31 crore. Firms with Rs 500 crore turnover can help design curricula and training to develop a skilled workforce tailored to regional industrial needs.

articles.headline: Undertrial prisoners booked for attempting to strangle warden in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Five undertrial prisoners accused of murder were booked for allegedly assaulting a warden at Parappana Agrahara Central Prison. The inmates reportedly pulled the warden into a barrack and tried to strangle him over a dispute involving checks on their belongings. An attempt to murder case was registered at the local police station following a complaint from jail authorities on Thursday.

articles.headline: Telangana CM Reddy battles internal party dissent after cabinet removals
articles.summary: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy faces growing friction within the Congress after the removal of two leaders for disciplinary violations. Minister Konda Surekha was ousted from the cabinet following disparaging remarks, while G Chinna Reddy lost his planning board post. Dissenters claim Reddy, a newcomer to the party, is excluding senior leaders from the state power structure.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh restores direct elections for mayors and municipal heads
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government passed a bill to restore direct elections for mayors and municipal chairpersons, ending a 21-year system of indirect votes. CM N Chandrababu Naidu said the move will stop frequent leadership changes and defections. The opposition YSRCP welcomed the change, viewing it as a test for the ruling coalition to maintain its hold in urban local body elections.

articles.headline: Telangana seeks Chhattisgarh NOC for Sammakka Sagar Godavari project
articles.summary: Telangana Irrigation Minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy requested a no-objection certificate from Chhattisgarh for the Sammakka Sagar Project. The barrage on the Godavari River requires the NOC to store water at its full reservoir level. Telangana promised to pay full compensation for any land or housing submerged in Chhattisgarh, aiming to realize the project's intended irrigation benefits.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu woman rescued from torture in Kuwait after viral video
articles.summary: Indian Embassy officials in Kuwait rescued a domestic worker named Vanitha after she posted a video detailing starvation and torture by her employers. Back in Tamil Nadu, police booked an employment agent for allegedly duping her. Vanitha confirmed her safety in a follow-up video from the embassy. Authorities are investigating the recruitment process that led to her overseas ordeal.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu farmers announce campaign against Mekedatu Dam project
articles.summary: Farmers' associations in Tamil Nadu will launch a five-day protest on September 20 against Karnataka's plan to build the Mekedatu Dam on the Cauvery. President P R Pandian called the project legally invalid and detrimental to agriculture in both states. Farmers urged the Centre to deny environmental clearances and suggested Rasimanal as a viable alternative for water storage.

articles.headline: Two arrested for providing mule bank accounts for cyber-fraud in Telangana
articles.summary: The TGCSB arrested two people in Khammam for providing 10 mule bank accounts used in cyber-fraud transactions. The accounts facilitated illegal online gaming payments and movement of funds coordinated with foreign Chinese operators. Simultaneous raids were conducted at multiple bank branches and ATM centres. Police have identified an organized local network involved in the scam.

articles.headline: Kerala cabinet starts strategic leadership retreat at IIM Kozhikode
articles.summary: Kerala Chief Minister VD Satheesan and his council of ministers began a two-day strategic retreat at IIM Kozhikode. Titled "Reimagining Kerala," the programme focuses on climate resilience, fiscal foundations, and higher education. Experts from global universities are leading sessions to improve cabinet coordination and expose ministers to new technological trends in governance.

articles.headline: Student groups clash at JNTU Hyderabad over inappropriate remarks
articles.summary: Police registered three cases after engineering students clashed at the JNTU Hyderabad campus. The fight, involving sticks, was sparked by inappropriate remarks made against a female student. Nineteen students were taken into custody and issued notices after the physical altercation and a subsequent protest at the university gate. One injured student was hospitalised for treatment.

articles.headline: Energy buys won't end Russia-Ukraine war, says EAM Jaishankar
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said the Russia-Ukraine conflict will only be resolved through diplomacy and dialogue, not by stopping commodity purchases like oil. Speaking in Warsaw, he reiterated that India has a responsibility to meet the energy needs of its 1.4 billion people. He called for intensified global efforts to support negotiations to bring the conflict to an end.

articles.headline: US fraud fugitive Manjit Singh Bedi arrested in Punjab
articles.summary: Punjab Police arrested Indian-origin fugitive Manjit Singh Bedi one day after he was added to the FBI's Most Wanted list. Bedi is accused of a $600,000 welfare benefits fraud scheme in Washington state. He had fled to India via Canada to avoid prosecution. The arrest follows an FBI reward offer of $150,000. Bedi allegedly ran an Asian grocery store used to defraud the SNAP program.

articles.headline: Registrar General issues circulars for complete enumeration in 2027 Census
articles.summary: The Registrar General of India directed census officers to count all settlements, including sailors, forest dwellers, and the homeless for the 2027 Census. Special attention will be given to rapid population growth areas and difficult terrains. Sailors on Indian mercantile ships will be enumerated if present at a domestic port on March 1, 2027. Training for defense census officers is also mandated.

articles.headline: Punjab government to hike Dearness Allowance to 60% for employees
articles.summary: The Punjab government announced an increase in Dearness Allowance from 42% to 60% for about 85,000 employees recruited after July 2020. The move aligns state salaries with the Central pay pattern. Minister Aman Arora said the recommendation from a cabinet sub-committee would be sent for final approval by the Chief Minister. The decision does not cover employees on older pay matrices.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi expands Chhatron ki Goonj student outreach to 800 districts
articles.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi will expand his student interaction programme to 800 districts ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. The initiative aims to engage Gen Z on issues like paper leaks and education costs. The first phase includes 28 episodes covering all states. The outreach follows a Congress Working Committee resolution to double down on engaging with India's youth.

articles.headline: Terrorist neutralised during joint security operation in Budgam
articles.summary: Security forces killed a terrorist during a joint operation by the Army, police, and CRPF in the Ashdar forests of central Kashmir's Budgam district. The operation was launched following specific intelligence on terrorist movement. An AK rifle and other war-like stores were recovered. The Army's 15 Corps confirmed that search operations in the region are still in progress.

articles.headline: Egg prices surge as ethanol demand inflates poultry feed costs
articles.summary: Retail egg prices across India have hit Rs 9 per piece as maize, a key feed ingredient, is diverted for ethanol blending. Feed costs have risen 25% since April, while maize prices increased from Rs 21,000 to Rs 27,000 per tonne. Poultry farmers are operating at reduced capacity and low margins, struggling to compete with the high demand for grains from the ethanol sector.

articles.headline: Grenade blast near Manipur Congress MLA's residence; no casualties
articles.summary: A suspected hand grenade exploded at the residential campus of Congress leader K Meghachandra Singh in Thoubal district. While no casualties were reported, police recovered a grenade lever from the site. CM Yumnam Khemchand condemned the attack. In a separate incident, a man was found shot dead in Imphal East. Police have registered cases and are investigating both violent incidents.

articles.headline: Ram Temple trust to consider deed changes for professional management
articles.summary: The Ayodhya Ram Temple trust will consider deed amendments on December 2 to restructure management for security and logistics. The changes follow the appointment of Air Marshal (retd) Jeetendra Mishra as the first CEO. The amendments aim to formalize the CEO's powers and improve transparency in fund management as the temple moves from construction to full-scale operation.

articles.headline: Kolkata teacher suspended for allegedly forcing student to remove tilak
articles.summary: A private school in Kolkata suspended a teacher for allegedly forcing a Class 5 student to wash off a sandalwood tilak. While the teacher claimed she only asked the boy to wash his face due to sweat smearing the mark, management suspended her pending a final decision. Opposition leader Suvendu Adhikari said a police case has been lodged against the teacher for the incident.

articles.headline: West Bengal fire department orders Abhishek Banerjee's office to vacate
articles.summary: The West Bengal fire department directed TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee to vacate two floors of a Camac Street building due to inadequate safety measures and an expired fire certificate. An audit found the occupancy posed an imminent threat to life and property. The move follows a team inspection of the premises, which are leased for the TMC's youth wing operations.

articles.headline: Two dead and one injured in Gorakhpur hit-and-run accident
articles.summary: A speeding truck killed two people and injured another in a series of collisions on the Ramkola-Padrauna road in Kushinagar district. The driver was attempting to flee after a previous accident. Local residents chased the vehicle, apprehended the driver, and handed him over to the police. The incident sparked local anger over speeding heavy vehicles on the district roads.

articles.headline: Nepal flood losses estimated at $2.56 billion; insurance claims rise
articles.summary: Nepal’s disaster authority reported property and infrastructure losses of $2.56 billion after last week's floods. The country must rebuild 20,000 houses and restore power to critical areas. Insurance claims worth over $171 million have been received, mainly from 11 damaged hydropower projects. Early recovery costs for immediate shelter and water are estimated at $52.6 million.

articles.headline: Houthis and Saudi-backed forces clash in Yemen; 129 killed
articles.summary: At least 129 people were killed in fierce clashes between Houthi rebels and Saudi-backed government forces in Yemen. The fighting erupted as rebels launched a ground and drone assault near the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait at the Red Sea. Military sources confirmed heavy casualties on both sides. The conflict highlights the ongoing instability near a major global oil chokepoint.

articles.headline: FSSAI tells court Dabur ignored warnings over 100% pure claims
articles.summary: The FSSAI informed the Delhi High Court that its restraining order against Dabur followed five improvement notices and multiple warnings since 2024. Dabur is barred from using "100% Pure" and "100% Natural" labels on food products. The regulator argued that the firm was given ample opportunity to take corrective measures and that the claims were misleading to consumers.

articles.headline: August e-way bills rise 7.7% signaling resilient goods movement
articles.summary: Electronic permit generation for goods shipment rose 7.7% year-on-year to 139.09 million in August. Although slightly lower than July, the figure stayed above the 130-million mark for the fifth straight month. Analysts state the trend signal economic resilience and improved GST compliance. The data is a key high-frequency indicator of domestic trade and consumption demand.

articles.headline: Low tariffs fuel surge in Chinese electric truck sales in India
articles.summary: Chinese automakers Sany and Foton are dominating India's electric heavy truck market, with Sany selling 722 units this fiscal year compared to five last year. Local manufacturers are concerned that a low 10% import duty on electric tractors gives foreign firms an unfair advantage. Indian executives are calling for higher tariffs to protect domestic firms investing in local R&D.

articles.headline: Sugar prices drop at mill gates but retail rates stay high
articles.summary: Ex-mill sugar prices have plunged over 23% to Rs 48 per kg following government action against hoarding, but retail prices have only fallen 4%. The retail average remains at Rs 62 per kg despite the sharp decline in wholesale costs. Industry experts expect retail prices to fall within the next 10 days as cheaper inventory moves through the supply chain to consumers.

articles.headline: JD Vance and Marco Rubio launch Foundry School for technical talent
articles.summary: US VP JD Vance and Marco Rubio announced "Foundry School," a training programme to rebuild domestic manufacturing. The initiative involves eight US universities and mentors from partner nations like India and Japan. Focusing on modern factory design and supply chains, the project aims to foster the high-tech talent needed for advanced manufacturing and assembly line engineering.

articles.headline: Tennis showman Gael Monfils bids farewell to Grand Slams
articles.summary: Gael Monfils played his final Grand Slam match at the US Open, losing to American Learner Tien in the second round. The 40-year-old Frenchman, known for his acrobatic athleticism and entertaining style, finishes a 22-season career with 13 ATP titles and 34 US Open wins. Monfils plans to transition into a coaching role for his wife, Elina Svitolina, and work in finance.

articles.headline: Aryna Sabalenka cruises into US Open fourth round with easy win
articles.summary: Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka defeated Kamilla Rakhimova 6-3, 6-4 to reach the US Open fourth round. The top seed fired four aces and saved four break points during the match. Sabalenka has now won 16 consecutive matches at Flushing Meadows. She is aiming to become the first woman since Serena Williams to win three straight US Open crowns.

articles.headline: Cafu says current Brazilian players lack national team identity
articles.summary: Legendary captain Cafu argued that young Brazilian players moving to Europe too early has weakened their identity with the national team. Speaking in Mumbai, the only player to play in three World Cup finals noted that previous winning squads were built on home-based talent. He emphasized that "Brasilidade" (Brazilianness) is missing from the current generation's play style.

articles.headline: Namal Rajapaksa arrested on corruption charges
articles.summary: Namal Rajapaksa, son of former Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapaksa, has been arrested on corruption charges linked to Airbus plane purchases by the national carrier, Sri Lankan Airlines.

articles.headline: Nation mourns Dolly Parton: Stars and Stripes flown at half-mast
articles.summary: America officially mourned singer Dolly Parton, flying the Stars and Stripes at half-mast across federal buildings, military installations, and diplomatic facilities, highlighting a national tribute to a non-politician.

articles.headline: Man stayed back to warn workers at flood-hit dam, rescued
articles.summary: Sanjay Sah, a mechanical foreman, was rescued alive after nine days in a flood-hit Nepal hydropower project tunnel, having stayed back to operate an alarm system and warn workers.

articles.headline: Near-simultaneous failure of all 3 hydraulic systems on A320neo
articles.summary: An Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's preliminary report confirmed a rare event where all three hydraulic systems of an A320neo aircraft failed within seconds, causing injuries to 24 flyers.

articles.headline: Wrestler, 2 kids die; dowry case filed
articles.summary: Former national-level wrestler Ashwini Pol and two of her children died after she jumped with them from a fort in Maharashtra. A dowry abuse case has been filed against her husband.

articles.headline: HC: Having separatist literature no ground for PSA detention
articles.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir High Court ruled that mere possession of books promoting separatist ideology is not grounds for preventive detention under the Public Safety Act.

articles.headline: Shooting coach faces abuse claims
articles.summary: A shooting coach, who travelled with the Indian team for Junior World Championships, faces sexual abuse allegations from junior rifle shooters.

articles.headline: No special treatment for cricketers at Asiad: IOA
articles.summary: The Indian Olympic Association stated that if cricketers need to stay outside official Asian Games hotels, the BCCI will be responsible for accommodation, food, and transport.

articles.headline: Isro fires 1st geo-imaging sat, sets GSLV payload record
articles.summary: Isro successfully launched EOS-05, India's first imaging satellite for geosynchronous orbit and its heaviest payload ever carried by a GSLV rocket, marking a comeback for the space agency.

articles.headline: Cops go slow on imposing curbs at key flyovers
articles.summary: Bengaluru traffic police are taking a graded approach to imposing restrictions on vehicles on key flyovers, with enforcement being uneven on Day One of the ban.

articles.headline: BMTC set to go 50% electric soon with 4.5k new e-buses
articles.summary: BMTC plans to induct 4,500 e-buses under the Centre's PM E-DRIVE scheme, expanding its fleet to nearly 11,000 buses in 18 months, aiming to reduce congestion and environmental benefits.

articles.headline: 5 inmates assault, try to strangle prison officer
articles.summary: Five prisoners at Central Prison, Parappana Agrahara, allegedly assaulted and attempted to strangle a warder after he confronted one of them over an earlier incident.

articles.headline: New Metro trains to give BMRCL chance to overhaul fleet
articles.summary: With four new trainsets for the Green Line expected, BMRCL will get an opportunity to undertake mid-life maintenance of its older rolling stock, improving operational flexibility.

articles.headline: DK Shivakumar: Not selling parks, need land for Metro
articles.summary: Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar defended the withdrawal of the Parks Amendment Bill, stating it was to facilitate discussion and not to sell parks, while ensuring land for the Namma Metro project.

articles.headline: 206 hearings completed, 43.8 lakh more to go for electoral roll revision
articles.summary: Bengaluru has completed 206 hearings for electoral roll revision, with 43.8 lakh voters statewide expected to receive notices. Booth-level officers, mostly teachers, are conducting the process.

articles.headline: Cloud-seeding operation launched to augment water availability
articles.summary: Karnataka launched a cloud-seeding operation using a specially equipped aircraft to augment water availability and protect farmers, despite facing a significant rainfall deficit.

articles.headline: Parameshwara: If economy is growing, where are jobs?
articles.summary: Karnataka Deputy CM G Parameshwara disputed the 7.8% GDP growth figure, questioning the lack of jobs and economic security for many citizens despite the economic growth.

articles.headline: Govt to seek stakeholder views on reforms in education
articles.summary: The Karnataka government plans to seek views from students, parents, and education experts before finalizing reforms in the education sector, focusing on KPSC recruitment and improving the system.

articles.headline: SPs don’t have power to extern persons under Police Act: HC
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court ruled that Superintendents of Police cannot exercise powers under Sections 55 and 56 of the Karnataka Police Act, concerning externment of individuals.

articles.headline: Drought list may expand as state reels under rain deficit
articles.summary: Karnataka may nearly double its drought-hit taluks from 101 to around 200 by the end of September due to severe water stress and a weak monsoon forecast.

articles.headline: Woman takes money for 2 yrs, robbed of gold chain worth 9L
articles.summary: A 33-year-old man accused his lover of attacking him with an iron object after she allegedly took money for two years and promised marriage, eventually robbing him of a gold chain worth Rs 9 lakh.

articles.headline: Bastar rock pushes India’s geological age back by 150m yrs
articles.summary: A rock slab in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, dated to 3.6 billion years ago, is India's oldest geological fragment, pushing its known rock record back by 150 million years.

articles.headline: MP HC acquits murder convict, censures special court judge
articles.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court acquitted a murder convict and passed strictures against a special court judge for errors in the trial, questioning his suitability for sensitive cases.

articles.headline: India reached other side of Moon but manual scavenging still prevalent: HC
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court lamented the prevalence of manual scavenging in India, contrasting it with space achievements and urging the implementation of the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act.

articles.headline: Train makes unscheduled halt to deliver milk to infant
articles.summary: The Sealdah-bound Darjeeling Mail made an unscheduled stop to deliver milk to an infant, despite running eight hours late and being diverted due to track subsidence.

articles.headline: Stray cattle fence proves fatal for father, son
articles.summary: A farmer and his son died of electrocution after an electrified fence around their crop, meant to deter stray cattle, came into contact with a main electricity line in UP.

articles.headline: Tribal woman assaulted, stripped in Rajasthan
articles.summary: Police arrested seven people in Rajasthan's Banswara after a tribal woman was allegedly assaulted, stripped, and had her head shaved in public by her husband and relatives.

articles.headline: Companies must create societal value, says ITC chairman
articles.summary: ITC Chairman Sanjiv Puri emphasized the need for companies to create economic and societal value beyond profit, adopting a 'triple bottom line' principle that includes environmental and social capital.

articles.headline: Isro achieved textbook mission, changing satellite orbit strategy
articles.summary: Isro successfully launched EOS-05, its first imaging satellite for geosynchronous orbit, by changing its satellite orbit strategy to continuously focus on the same region.

articles.headline: RBI says India's forex reserves hit record high of $741 billion
articles.summary: India's forex reserves jumped $11.5 billion to a new all-time high of $741 billion during the week ended August 28, the RBI said, with geopolitical tensions contributing to the rise.

articles.headline: ByteDance lands $29.6bn loan as AI investments drive interest
articles.summary: ByteDance secured a $29.6 billion loan from nearly 30 banks, fueled by its bet on AI development and strong interest from lenders, making it the second-largest loan in Asia this year.

articles.headline: HUL plans capex boost; eyes entry into new spaces
articles.summary: Hindustan Unilever (HUL) will increase capital expenditure to 3% of turnover from 2% and enter select high-growth spaces, leveraging new D2C brand acquisitions and improving distribution channels.

articles.headline: As protein demand rises, brands go for smaller packs
articles.summary: As protein demand grows in India, brands are offering smaller, affordable protein packs to make them more accessible and fit into convenient snacking occasions, catering to health-conscious consumers.

articles.headline: US Open: Zverev wins another five-setter, Sabalenka sails through
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev won his second consecutive five-setter at the US Open, while Aryna Sabalenka advanced easily, as other top seeds like Alex de Minaur were eliminated.

articles.headline: Cafu: India can gain from playing football giants like Brazil
articles.summary: Brazilian football legend Cafu believes India can gain significantly from playing football giants like Brazil, stating that modern football sees teams playing on equal terms, regardless of rankings.

articles.headline: BCCI plans to turn Sooryavanshi's promise into lasting greatness like Tendulkar's
articles.summary: The BCCI is closely monitoring 15-year-old prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, aiming to nurture his career for longevity like Sachin Tendulkar, focusing on cautious development steps.

articles.headline: Siraj needs Duleep final to find rhythm, says former selector
articles.summary: Former national selector Devang Gandhi believes Mohammed Siraj needs the Duleep Trophy final to regain rhythm and utilize his wobble seam ability, advising him to be judicious about his pace.

articles.headline: Bombay HC orders takedown of Shruti Haasan deepfakes
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court directed social media platforms to remove objectionable content against Shruti Haasan, stating she made a strong prima facie case for protection of her personality rights.

articles.headline: Karnataka cabinet withdraws controversial parkland bill
articles.summary: The Karnataka Cabinet withdrew the controversial Parks (Preservation) Amendment Bill, 2026, allowing public discussion on using park land for infrastructure, following widespread opposition.

articles.headline: Swara Bhaskar clarifies 'problematic' remark on Padmaavat's jauhar
articles.summary: Swara Bhaskar clarified her statement on the jauhar scene in 'Padmaavat', explaining she meant it was problematic to imply survivors were cowards, not that Rani Padmavati herself was cowardly.

articles.headline: Limp Bizkit, Olivia Dean & Katseye headed to India for festival
articles.summary: Global rock act Limp Bizkit and singers Olivia Dean and Katseye are confirmed headliners for the upcoming Lollapalooza India festival, joined by a mix of international and Indian artistes.

articles.headline: Mistaken identities and mayhem make for uneven crime comedy
articles.summary: 'Jeevan Ya Bheema Con?', a crime comedy starring Arshad Warsi, suffers from a weak screenplay and forced humour, despite strong performances from its lead actors.

articles.headline: A fantasy film that never takes off
articles.summary: 'The Magic Faraway Tree', a fantasy film, has colourful characters and a good cast but fails to capture the book's wonder, with its adventures feeling designed and the family story underdeveloped.

articles.headline: A messy, but entertaining, mass supernatural ride
articles.summary: 'I'm Game', a Malayalam supernatural entertainer starring Dulquer Salmaan, offers enjoyable fantasy, humour, and action in the first half, but its lengthy runtime causes lags.

articles.headline: Ravi Kishan steals spotlight in this fan-service entertainer
articles.summary: 'Mirzapur: The Movie' revisits the crime drama's world but falters in the second half. Pankaj Tripathi is excellent, and Ravi Kishan is a strong addition, but the film overstays its welcome.

articles.headline: When your professor pops up on your feed
articles.summary: Professors are increasingly using social media to connect with students, share insights, and understand their interests, bridging the gap and creating a more informal learning environment.

articles.headline: Gen Z is ghosting the Instagram grid
articles.summary: Gen Z users are utilizing Instagram's archive tool for 'ghost-posting,' uploading and then archiving content to reclaim autonomy over their online presence and create personal moodboards.

articles.headline: India's Gen Z turns to AI for upskilling amid burnout concerns
articles.summary: 82% of India's Gen Z use AI for upskilling, but 60% report burnout from the pressure to continuously learn. Studying abroad is also losing appeal due to costs and visa uncertainty.

articles.headline: Ranjit Kumar & Lokesh Kashyap
articles.summary: Mirabai Chanu shares her bond with coach Vijay Sharma, highlighting trust, understanding, and family. Sharma sees Mirabai as his child, and she has taught him patience.

articles.headline: Gloria Steinem: Champion of women's rights, passes away at 92
articles.summary: Gloria Steinem, a prominent feminist and journalist who championed women's rights, passed away at 92. Her activism significantly influenced greater rights for women globally.

articles.headline: Sooraj Pancholi addresses Disha Salian death probe again
articles.summary: Actor Sooraj Pancholi denied knowing Disha Salian and requested not to be 'dragged into this without any proof', stating he wants her father to get justice but doesn't want to be a soft target.

articles.headline: ISRO successfully launches EOS-05 imaging satellite aboard GSLV-F17 rocket
articles.summary: ISRO launched its first successful mission of the year, placing the EOS-05 geo-imaging satellite into orbit from Sriharikota. The 2,367kg satellite is the heaviest ever launched by a GSLV and will provide near real-time monitoring of cyclones, cloudbursts, and agriculture. PM Modi lauded the achievement as a reflection of India's growing capabilities in the global space sector.

articles.headline: Air India A320 lost all hydraulics mid-flight; captain tested positive for drugs
articles.summary: An Air India Airbus A320neo lost all three hydraulic systems at 36,000 feet on August 4, causing a violent altitude upset that injured 24 people. A preliminary AAIB report found the pilot-in-command tested non-negative for a psycho-active substance. The aircraft gained 372 feet and fell 292 feet within seconds. Technical investigations into the triple system failure are still underway.

articles.headline: Anil Chakravarthy to lead Adobe as new President & CEO
articles.summary: Adobe has named Indian-origin Anil Chakravarthy as its next president and CEO, succeeding Shantanu Narayen from December 1. Chakravarthy has been instrumental in AI development at Adobe.

articles.headline: No tax tangle, FPIs keen to move G-Sec funds next day
articles.summary: Foreign portfolio investors want to remit funds a day after selling government securities, proposing quarterly letters instead of daily ones to streamline the process post-tax exemption.

articles.headline: 275 Indians missing in Nepal after deadly flash floods
articles.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs confirmed that 275 Indian nationals remain missing in Nepal following massive floods and glacial collapses. India has rescued 169 citizens and safely evacuated nearly 2,000 from China. India has sent 54 personnel and 95 tonnes of relief materials to support Nepal. The disaster has killed over 1,280 people and devastated Himalayan hydropower infrastructure.

articles.headline: Influencer detained over bragging about cracking skull
articles.summary: Hindutva influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj was detained for allegedly bragging about cracking a student's father's skull and getting away with it due to political connections. The incident sparked protests.

articles.headline: Karnataka CM to meet PM seeking farm loan relief
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar will lead an all-party delegation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi to seek a waiver of farm loans amid drought conditions in over 100 taluks.

articles.headline: HarperCollins India to publish Sonia Gandhi memoir Belonging on November 10
articles.summary: HarperCollins India will publish Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, "Belonging: A Visual Journey of Love," ending uncertainty after a deal with Penguin Random House reportedly fell through. Gandhi allegedly refused to edit references to PM Modi and the RSS. The book traces her life from Italy to India, her personal losses, and her political journey leading the Congress party for two decades.

articles.headline: India favourites against Pakistan in Asia Cup; focus on cricket: Mithali
articles.summary: Former India captain Mithali Raj urged the team to focus on cricket and block out the noise during the India vs Pakistan Asia Cup match, highlighting the importance of role clarity.

articles.headline: SAI builds container prototypes for Asian Games athlete acclimatisation
articles.summary: The Sports Authority of India developed shipping container living quarters in Patiala and Bengaluru to prepare athletes for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. In Japan, athletes will stay in temporary container-based housing on a cruise ship. The prototypes help competitors adjust to compact living spaces and prevent claustrophobia, ensuring their focus remains on performance and mental state.

articles.headline: White House unveils 'MAGA' video games
articles.summary: The White House launched five retro-style video games on its website, themed around President Trump's MAGA agenda, including 'Build the Wall' and 'Rio Run', sparking controversy over their immigration policy overtones.

articles.headline: FCNR dollar flows test RBI's liquidity toolkit
articles.summary: FCNR dollar inflows are putting the RBI's liquidity management toolkit to the test. The central bank needs to manage excess liquidity effectively to maintain financial stability.

articles.headline: US yields, rate jitters drag Indian equities
articles.summary: Rising US yields and rate jitters are causing a downturn in Indian equities, leading to a market close below last week's level. Investors are adopting a cautious stance.

articles.headline: Chinese truckmakers lead in India's EV race
articles.summary: Chinese truck manufacturers are establishing a dominant position in India's burgeoning electric vehicle market, driven by technological advancements and competitive pricing strategies.

articles.headline: Tata Trusts, Singh differ over 'unbecoming' remark
articles.summary: An apparent disagreement has surfaced between Tata Trusts and an individual named Singh concerning a remark attributed to the charity commissioner.

articles.headline: Indian Spy satellite surveillance flights on ISRO's agenda
articles.summary: ISRO is planning to launch Indian spy satellite surveillance missions to enhance national security and monitoring capabilities, strengthening India's observational capacity.

articles.headline: Battery storage mandatory for RITES projects from July 2021
articles.summary: RITES has mandated battery storage systems for all its projects commencing July 2021, promoting renewable energy utilization and grid stability.

articles.headline: Subscriber growth gives VI room to flex creative muscle
articles.summary: Increased subscriber numbers are empowering VI (Vodafone Idea) to enhance its creative offerings and service capabilities, signalling a positive strategic shift.

articles.headline: Adults only: violent films lose family viewers
articles.summary: Violent films are losing family viewership, with a shift towards more family-friendly content. This trend impacts box office collections and film distribution strategies.

articles.headline: Bajaj's Bajaj opts for steady growth over rapid spread
articles.summary: Bajaj Finance is focusing on a strategy of sustained growth rather than rapid expansion, emphasizing market consolidation and operational efficiency.

articles.headline: Q-comms crisis 'quality cops' as scrutiny up
articles.summary: The quick commerce sector faces challenges related to quality control and compliance, prompting increased regulatory scrutiny and the hiring of 'quality cops'.

articles.headline: Aug E-way bills touch 77% to over 139 mn
articles.summary: August saw a significant increase in e-way bills, reaching over 139 million. This surge indicates robust economic activity and improved tax compliance across sectors.

articles.headline: HUL to step up Capex for volume-led gains
articles.summary: Hindustan Unilever Ltd (HUL) plans to increase capital expenditure (Capex) to drive volume-led growth. The company aims to achieve better efficiency and cost savings.

articles.headline: SEBI clears National Stock Exchange for long-awaited initial public offering
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India approved the IPO for the National Stock Exchange (NSE), ending a decade of delays. NSE's listing was previously stalled by the co-location scandal and leadership changes. The exchange settled with SEBI for Rs 1,300 crore earlier this year. The offering is expected to be valued at over Rs 5 lakh crore, entirely as an offer for sale by shareholders.

articles.headline: Why our mangoes, the world's best, fall in a unique export market
articles.summary: Indian mangoes, renowned globally for their quality, face challenges in the export market due to stringent regulations and competition. Efforts are underway to streamline export processes.

articles.headline: RBI curbs push some traders to tap client shares
articles.summary: Recent RBI restrictions are prompting some market participants to utilize client shares, raising questions about regulatory adherence and market integrity.

articles.headline: Telcos, quality norms facing scrutiny
articles.summary: Telecom operators are under scrutiny regarding their adherence to quality norms, with regulatory bodies assessing service standards and customer satisfaction.

articles.headline: Quick commerce firms hire 'quality cops' as scrutiny ups
articles.summary: Quick commerce firms are hiring 'quality cops' amid increased regulatory scrutiny. This move aims to ensure compliance and improve operational standards.

articles.headline: Why Indian hockey needs a shakeup
articles.summary: Indian hockey is in need of a drastic reform to revive its past glory. The article examines the current state of the sport and suggests improvements.

articles.headline: Bringing the human touch into science
articles.summary: The article explores the importance of human touch and empathy in scientific research and education, emphasizing the role of social sciences in scientific progress.

articles.headline: Revisiting 7 underrated Agatha Christie novels
articles.summary: A look at seven lesser-known Agatha Christie novels that deserve more recognition. The article delves into their plots and literary significance.

articles.headline: Vassani's track traces the rise and fall of kingdoms
articles.summary: M.G. Vassani's book 'The Apparition' delves into the rise and fall of kingdoms, exploring themes of power, history, and human nature.

articles.headline: 'Why am I so tired' and other stuff we ask Google
articles.summary: This article examines common queries people submit to Google, such as 'Why am I so tired?', reflecting contemporary concerns and information-seeking behavior.

articles.headline: Gaggan brings Raga to Delhi
articles.summary: Chef Gaggan Anand is bringing his signature culinary style, inspired by Indian classical music (Raga), to Delhi, offering a unique dining experience.

articles.headline: Donald Trump threatens to halt trade if Federal Reserve maintains high rates
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened to cease trading with countries that have a trade deficit with America if the Federal Reserve does not lower interest rates. Trump claimed high rates place the US at a "very unfair disadvantage" and cited a Supreme Court decision as precedent for his authority to block trade. He argued these measures are more effective than traditional tariffs.

articles.headline: Bengaluru resort kitchen sealed after raid finds expired chilli and labels
articles.summary: Food safety officials sealed the kitchen of Chairman’s Club resort in Sahakaranagar after finding 40 kg of expired chilli and prohibited artificial colours. Inspectors reported poor hygiene, cross-contamination risks between vegetarian and non-vegetarian storage, and missing labels on breadcrumbs. The raid was part of a state-wide inspection drive led by the health department.

articles.headline: Global Chess League begins in Bengaluru with Carlsen and Anand
articles.summary: The fourth season of the Global Chess League starts Saturday in Bengaluru, featuring legends Magnus Carlsen and Viswanathan Anand. Six teams will compete in a double round-robin format with unique board structures and fast-paced time controls. New features include heart-rate monitors for captains and live app streams allowing fans to test moves against world-class grandmasters.

articles.headline: Satwik-Chirag reach China Masters semi-finals after gruelling win
articles.summary: India's Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty defeated Denmark’s Kim Astrup and Anders Rasmussen to enter the China Masters semi-finals. The fourth-seeded pair won a 70-minute thriller 21-13, 16-21, 21-18. While the duo continues their strong 2026 run, veteran Kidambi Srikanth's campaign ended with a loss in the men’s singles quarter-finals on Friday.

articles.headline: BCCI bans Bengal spinner Rohit Yadav for age fraud
articles.summary: The BCCI imposed a two-year ban on leg-spinner Rohit Yadav for age fraud. The decision comes shortly after Yadav was selected for India's U-19 squad for an upcoming series against Australia. Yadav, who represents Bengal but is from UP, had previously played for India U-19 in Sri Lanka. The ban prevents him from participating in any official cricket activities for the duration.

articles.headline: Belgian PM: Europe was slow to heed Modi's warning on dependency
articles.summary: Belgian PM Bart De Wever stated Europe was slow to recognise the risks of economic dependency, admitting PM Modi had warned them earlier, but they are listening now.

articles.headline: Banks need to rethink their approach to Gen Z
articles.summary: Gen Z, a significant demographic for banks, prefers mobile-first, fast, and seamless experiences. Banks must adapt to this digital-first approach to remain relevant.
